grammarPoints.title: Personal endings with -im / -sin (to be)
grammarPoints.explanation: Turkish often attaches the verb 'to be' as a personal suffix: iyiyim (I am fine), nasılsın (how are you).

grammarPoints.title: Vowel harmony basics
grammarPoints.explanation: Suffix vowels often match front/back harmony of the stem (e.g. kitap-ta, ev-de).

grammarPoints.title: Yes/no questions with mi/mı/mu/mü
grammarPoints.explanation: Yes/no questions use a separate particle that follows vowel harmony: Güzel mi? — Is it nice?

grammarPoints.title: Wanting with istemek
grammarPoints.explanation: Use object + istiyorum to say what you want: Bir çay istiyorum.

grammarPoints.title: Locative case -de/-da
grammarPoints.explanation: Location is marked with -de/-da (and variants): evde (at home), otelde (at the hotel).

grammarPoints.title: Present continuous -iyor
grammarPoints.explanation: Ongoing actions use -iyor plus personal endings: çalışıyorum, okuyorum.

grammarPoints.title: Giving opinions with bence
grammarPoints.explanation: Start opinions with bence (in my opinion), then a full clause.

grammarPoints.title: Talking about abstract topics
grammarPoints.explanation: B2 topics use abstract nouns (özgürlük, sorumluluk) with stance verbs (inanmak, tartışmak).
